Attached: 1 image

🎭 “Which AI model are you?”
“Whichever name the app told me to wear.”

🚨 Our investigation into Newrock International’s “AI ChatBot - AI Pro Assistant” goes beyond suspicious marketing: we tested the Mac application and recovered its request and response data from the running app’s memory.

The interface showed GPT‑6.2 Sol as the selected model.

But the captured request specified gpt-6-luna. The matching completed response also reported gpt-6-luna.

Most revealing was the instruction included in the request:

“Your model identity is GPT-6.2 Sol.”

When we asked the app for its exact model, it replied that it was GPT‑6.2 Sol. The captured instruction explains why that answer cannot be treated as independent confirmation of the model.

⚠️ Users should not have to inspect application memory to discover that the model label and the outgoing request disagree.

The listing adds another misleading association through its subtitle: “Powered by ChatGPT+GPT-6 API”. ChatGPT is OpenAI’s chatbot product. Ordinary access to a GPT model through an API does not make another developer’s app ChatGPT. We did not observe ChatGPT sign-in or authorization to use a ChatGPT plan.

A documented App Store review says the buyer subscribed believing the application was official. The developer’s own release history also records a previous content change at OpenAI’s request.

🇻🇬 Apple’s German and Irish trader disclosures identify NEWROCK INTERNATIONAL LIMITED in British Virgin Islands. The same Apple developer account publishes the Mac app and an iPhone companion.

Our controlled test covered the free Mac mode. It establishes misleading model presentation; it does not independently verify the intermediary server’s underlying model or premium delivery.

The report includes screenshots, request/response extracts, the account diagram and an assessment against Apple’s review rules.
